items.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023
items.q: I even saw a guy who was working with Phil Ramone on a production at A&R slice just a square out of a 24-track tape.

ctx.x: I had a moment in the studio once, I wonder if you had a moment like this. The first time I saw tape sliced with a razor blade and hooked back together I said what is that? This actually works?

Yeah. No it was amazing. There’s some great tape operators and engineers who were amazing with a razor blade and it’s a crucial, very scary moment when you see the razor blade cut the 24-track tape or 16-track tape back in the days, and then put it back together. And oh my God, it sounds okay. I even saw a guy who was working with Phil Ramone on a production at A&R slice just a square out of a 24-track tape. So not just a © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-
razor blade but like an Exacto knife — like a little quarter inch square of tape and then replace that. Somebody hit a microphone or something and there was no other way to repair it than that.
